title: A Short History of Computing (HIST 2310 reading)

facts.fact: The word computer originally referred to a person who carried out calculations.
facts.quote: the word computer originally referred to a person

facts.fact: John Napier published logarithms in 1614.
facts.quote: Logarithms, published by John Napier in 1614

facts.fact: Blaise Pascal built the Pascaline adding machine in 1642.
facts.quote: Blaise Pascal built an adding machine, later called the Pascaline, in 1642

facts.fact: Leibniz's calculator used a stepped drum.
facts.quote: using a stepped drum

facts.fact: The Difference Engine project was abandoned in 1833.
facts.quote: the project was abandoned in 1833

facts.fact: The Science Museum completed a Difference Engine No. 2 in 1991.
facts.quote: constructed by the Science Museum in London and completed in 1991

facts.fact: The Analytical Engine separated a store holding numbers from a mill performing arithmetic.
facts.quote: Its design separated a store, which held numbers, from a mill, which performed arithmetic on them

facts.fact: Ada Lovelace's Note G described computing the Bernoulli numbers on the Analytical Engine.
facts.quote: In the last of these notes, Note G, she described in detail how the engine could compute the Bernoulli numbers

facts.fact: Hollerith's tabulator used pins passing through holes into mercury to complete a circuit.
facts.quote: a pin passed through into a cup of mercury and completed an electrical circuit

facts.fact: The combined company was renamed International Business Machines in 1924.
facts.quote: in 1924 the combined company was renamed International Business Machines

facts.fact: Vannevar Bush's differential analyser was completed in 1931.
facts.quote: completed in 1931

facts.fact: Zuse's Z3 of 1941 was built from about 2,600 telephone relays.
facts.quote: built from about 2,600 telephone relays

facts.fact: The first Colossus was designed by Tommy Flowers and contained about 1,600 vacuum tubes.
facts.quote: It contained about 1,600 vacuum tubes

facts.fact: ENIAC contained about 18,000 vacuum tubes and could perform about 5,000 additions per second.
facts.quote: It could perform about 5,000 additions per second

facts.fact: Von Neumann wrote the First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC in June 1945.
facts.quote: In June 1945 von Neumann wrote the First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC

facts.fact: The Manchester Baby ran its first program on 21 June 1948.
facts.quote: It ran its first program on 21 June 1948

facts.fact: EDSAC ran its first program on 6 May 1949.
facts.quote: EDSAC ran its first program on 6 May 1949

facts.fact: UNIVAC predicted Eisenhower's landslide on CBS in 1952.
facts.quote: it predicted a landslide victory for Dwight Eisenhower

facts.fact: About 2,000 IBM 650 computers were installed.
facts.quote: with about 2,000 installed

facts.fact: FORTRAN was developed at IBM by a team led by John Backus and released in 1957.
facts.quote: developed at IBM by a team led by John Backus and released in 1957

facts.fact: The transistor was invented at Bell Laboratories in 1947 by Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley.
facts.quote: invented at Bell Laboratories in 1947 by John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley

facts.fact: In 1975 Moore revised his prediction to a doubling about every two years.
facts.quote: In 1975 he revised the rate to a doubling about every two years

facts.fact: The Intel 4004 of 1971 contained about 2,300 transistors.
facts.quote: The 4004 contained about 2,300 transistors

facts.fact: IBM's 305 RAMAC of 1956 stored about five megabytes on fifty platters.
facts.quote: used fifty spinning metal platters

facts.fact: The System/360 made the 8-bit byte the standard unit of computer memory.
facts.quote: The System/360 also made the 8-bit byte the standard unit of computer memory

facts.fact: Brooks's law says adding programmers to a late software project makes it later.
facts.quote: adding programmers to a late software project makes it later

facts.fact: Edgar F. Codd proposed the relational model of data in 1970.
facts.quote: In 1970 Edgar F. Codd

facts.fact: The ARPANET switched to TCP/IP on 1 January 1983.
facts.quote: The ARPANET switched to TCP/IP on 1 January 1983

facts.fact: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989.
facts.quote: The World Wide Web was proposed in 1989 by Tim Berners-Lee

facts.fact: The Morris worm began spreading on 2 November 1988.
facts.quote: On 2 November 1988 a program written by Robert Tappan Morris

facts.fact: The Advanced Encryption Standard replaced DES in 2001.
facts.quote: it was replaced in 2001 by the Advanced Encryption Standard

facts.fact: Linus Torvalds began writing the Linux kernel in 1991.
facts.quote: In 1991 Linus Torvalds, a student at the University of Helsinki, began writing a kernel

facts.fact: The term artificial intelligence was coined by John McCarthy for the 1956 Dartmouth workshop.
facts.quote: The term artificial intelligence was coined by John McCarthy

facts.fact: Seymour Cray's CDC 6600 of 1964 was the fastest computer in the world for several years.
facts.quote: His CDC 6600 of 1964 was the fastest computer in the world for several years

facts.fact: The TOP500 list has been published twice a year since 1993.
facts.quote: The TOP500 list, published twice a year since 1993

facts.fact: In 2022 Frontier at Oak Ridge became the first machine on the TOP500 list to exceed one exaflop.
facts.quote: In 2022 the Frontier supercomputer at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the United States became the first machine on the list to exceed one exaflop
